text: My dentist's office called and moved my cleaning to Tuesday the twenty first at eight thirty in the morning instead of the afternoon. Could you add that to my calendar and maybe text my boss, Diane, that I'll be in around ten that day? I don't want to forget and end up missing my standup.

Last night I went to see my nephew's band play at a bar downtown called The Copper Lantern. They're called Static Orchard, which I still don't understand, and there were maybe thirty people there. Eli plays bass and he barely looked up the whole set, but during the last song he did a solo and the room actually went quiet. Afterward the bartender told me they've been booked for every second Friday through December. I bought a t-shirt even though it's two sizes too big.

I run a small bookstore in Asheville and foot traffic has dropped about twenty percent since the new shopping center opened. I've got one employee, Margo, and a back room that's mostly empty. I'm wondering what kinds of events could bring people in on weeknights without costing me much. What would you try? The store is on Lexington Avenue, about two blocks from the brewery, and our regulars are mostly retirees and a few college students. I tried a poetry night once in the spring and four people came, two of which were Margo's parents. I'd like to try something that feels more social, maybe something with the brewery crowd, but I'm not sure where to start.

Can you text my brother Sam and tell him the barbecue moved to Sunday? Mom's hip is acting up so we pushed it. Actually, while I'm thinking about mom, she mentioned the physical therapist wants her doing exercises three times a day and she's maybe doing them once. I don't know how to motivate her without nagging.

I just got out of the hardware store and I swear I went in for a single furnace filter, the sixteen by twenty five one, and came out with a cordless drill, a bag of birdseed and a tomato cage. And speaking of tomatoes, the ones in the backyard are finally turning red after all that rain, which honestly surprised me.

What was the name of that book I mentioned last week, the one about the woman who walks the Pacific Crest Trail after her mom dies? Not Wild, the other one. I think it was by someone Australian. Anyway, my book club is picking titles for spring and I want to suggest it. Also, did I ever tell you what Janice picked last time? It was terrible.

Remember that summer I spent at the lake house in Wisconsin when I was twelve? I was thinking about it today because the smell of the pine trees at the trailhead brought it all back. My uncle Frank taught me to fish off the dock, and we caught a northern pike that he swore was the biggest one on the lake. He's been gone for eight years now. Anyway, it got me thinking about how I want my own kids to have summers like that. They're always on screens. Maybe next year we rent a cabin somewhere for a week, no wifi. Although my oldest would probably mutiny. Speaking of which, I need to talk to her about her phone time, it's out of control.

My grandmother had this recipe box with handwritten cards, and when she passed, my aunt took it. I keep meaning to ask her to scan them. There's one for apricot kolaches that nobody else knows how to make, and I'm afraid it'll just get lost. Grandma never measured anything, so half the cards just say a handful or until it looks right. I should probably call my aunt this weekend and just ask. I don't know why I keep putting it off.

Well, last night was exciting. The wind was howling, the power flickered three times, and the kids all ended up in our bed by two in the morning. Our neighbor's tree came down in the storm last night and landed half on our fence. Nobody got hurt, thank goodness, but the fence is flattened along about twenty feet, and the dog has already figured out he can walk right into their yard. We talked this morning and he was very apologetic. He says his homeowner's insurance should cover it, and he gave me his agent's name and number. Could you save that his insurance agent is Linda Park at five five five, two one nine, four four eight zero.

I'm just so tired of this commute. Forty five minutes each way on the 405 and today some guy in a white pickup cut me off twice. And honestly it's not even the traffic, it's that I spend ninety minutes a day in a car when I could be with the kids. Which reminds me, Sophie's science project is due Monday and we haven't even picked a topic. She wants to do something with slime. I don't know what slime proves.

So we've been touring daycares for a month now, and I've seen some things. One had a ball pit that smelled like old cheese, and another had a two year waitlist, which I think means they want you to apply before the baby exists. We just finished the walkthrough of the new daycare and I'm feeling a lot better about it. The rooms were clean, the staff seemed calm, and they have a real garden where the kids plant tomatoes. My son immediately ran to the sandbox and refused to leave, which I'm taking as a good sign. The director answered every question we had, even the weird ones about nap schedules. Anyway, please make a note that the daycare deposit of two hundred dollars is due by the fifth.

Earlier this month I told you about the plumber we used for the water heater, the one my neighbor Rosa recommended. I think I said he was really fair on price and showed up on time. Now the upstairs toilet is running nonstop, and I'd rather call him than some random company off the internet. Do you remember his name or the company he worked for? I think it had the word Brothers in it, but I'm not sure.

I finally took my daughter Priya to her first swim meet this morning. She was so nervous she wouldn't eat breakfast. She swam the fifty meter freestyle in lane four and came in third, and the look on her face when she saw the board was everything. Her coach, Mr. Delgado, gave her a high five.

My father in law was a radio operator in the Navy during Korea, and he keeps telling this story about bouncing signals off the ionosphere to talk to ships hundreds of miles away. I nodded along but I don't actually understand how that works. Why do some radio waves bounce off the atmosphere and others go right through it? And is that why AM stations come in from farther away at night?

My wife and I were talking about our anniversary, and she mentioned, very casually, that she's always wanted to go to the lighthouse restaurant up the coast. She said it like it was nothing, but I know that tone. Twenty years of marriage teaches you things. Put that in my notes, the lighthouse restaurant is what she wants for our anniversary. I also need to figure out who can watch the kids that weekend, but that's a problem for later me. My sister owes me one, so I might call in that favor.

So I finally went back to the gym after six months of paying for nothing, and the guy at the front desk didn't even recognize me, which was humbling. They moved all the machines around too. I'm on the treadmill at the gym and the TV is showing a cooking competition, somebody is making a soufflé in twelve minutes, which seems impossible. I tried a soufflé once in college, it collapsed, my roommate ate it anyway with a spoon straight out of the dish. She's a lawyer now in Chicago. We should catch up. Anyway the trainer just walked by and told me my new routine, so save that it's three sets of twelve on legs Monday and Thursday.

My grandfather emigrated from Sicily in 1921 and came through Ellis Island. My aunt has his naturalization papers, and they list his name as Salvatore but everyone always called him Sam. I'm curious how the immigration process actually worked back then. Did officials really change people's names at Ellis Island like everyone says, or is that a myth? And how long did it usually take someone to become a citizen in the twenties?

I need to remember to stop leaving my reading glasses in the car, honestly. That's the third time this week. Note to self I guess. Anyway, I'm on my way to the eye doctor, which is ironic, and I'm thinking about whether to finally get progressives. My optometrist, Dr. Liang, has been pushing them for two years now. She says they'd help with night driving, which has gotten worse since I turned fifty. Honestly the cost scares me more than anything. Last time my glasses were almost four hundred dollars with the coating. Oh, and the parking garage by her office is closed for repairs, so I'll be circling the block for a while. Fantastic.

Okay so I'm walking the dog and I'm still annoyed about the meeting this morning. Kevin presented my analysis to the vice president like it was his own work, the whole retention model, the slide with the cohort chart, all of it. And I just sat there. I didn't say anything. And I keep thinking, why didn't I say anything? Probably because I'm still new and I don't want to be that person. But it's also not the first time. Anyway, the dog just found a squirrel and nearly pulled my arm off. And the leaves are turning, which is nice. I keep telling myself fall is my favorite season and then I spend all of it indoors staring at spreadsheets. Maybe this weekend I'll actually go up to the lake.

I can't believe how much the school fundraiser has taken over my life. I volunteered to run the silent auction because nobody else would, and now I have forty two items to catalog, a spreadsheet that keeps breaking, and a principal who emails me at six in the morning. The event is November eighteenth at the gym. Every parent I talk to says they'll donate something and then nothing shows up. I'm proud of what we're building, but I'm running on fumes and I've snapped at my kids twice this week because of it. Maybe next year I'll just say no when they ask. Or at least ask for a co-chair.

We had the neighborhood block party on Saturday and it went way better than I expected. The Hendersons brought a whole smoked brisket, the kids from number twelve set up a lemonade stand, and old Mr. Patel told everyone the story of how he built his house in nineteen seventy one with his brothers.

We're thinking about putting solar panels on the house. The roof faces south, we're in central Ohio, and our electric bill runs about a hundred and forty dollars a month. How long does it usually take for panels to pay for themselves around here, and does snow on the roof in winter make a big difference? My neighbor Frank put panels on two years ago and claims he hasn't paid an electric bill since, but Frank also exaggerates about everything, so I'm not sure I believe him. We plan to stay in this house at least another fifteen years, and I've heard there's a federal tax credit, though I don't know if it's still around or how much it covers.

I need to wake up an hour early tomorrow for the hospital shift swap. I'm usually up at six, so I need to be up at five, and I need a second alarm at five ten because I'm not a morning person. Can you set those for me? I'm covering for my coworker Jenna because her kid has the flu, and if I'm late the whole floor feels it. I'd also love it if you could text her and tell her I've got it covered and not to worry.

Our accountant finally got back to me about the taxes. Apparently we can deduct part of the home office this year, but only if I keep receipts for anything I buy for it, which I have not been doing. She was nice about it, but I could hear her sighing through the phone. She also said the new rules on the child care credit changed again, and she walked me through it twice, and I understood it maybe once. Hang on to this for me: I need to send her the mileage log and the daycare receipts by February fifteenth. Otherwise she files an extension, and she charges extra for that, and I already pay her more than I pay for groceries in a month. I'm going to start a folder in the glove box for receipts. That's the plan. We'll see how long it lasts.

Do you remember what I told you about my son's allergy medicine? The pediatrician changed the dose a while back and I mentioned it to you then. I'm at the pharmacy now, and I want to make sure the refill they're giving me matches what she said. I think she switched him from the chewable to the liquid, and I remember something about giving it at night instead of in the morning. The pharmacist is asking me if anything changed and I just froze. He's seven now, and he's had the same prescription since he was four, so I just want to be sure I'm not mixing it up with the old instructions.

If seven thirty isn't available, anything between seven and eight works. Also, could you text my wife to let her know it's done once you book it? She's been asking me all week.

Just finished lunch with my old college roommate, Jen, first time in like five years. She has twins now, she lives out by the lake, and she's training for a triathlon, which makes me tired just thinking about it. We talked about everyone from the dorm, who got married, who moved abroad, who's mysteriously off social media. Apparently Derek runs a goat yoga studio now, which I have so many questions about. She also recommended a financial advisor who helped her a lot after her divorce. Keep track of the fact that Jen's advisor is Marcus Bell at Northpoint Financial, and she says to mention her name when I call. Then we split a dessert and talked about our parents getting older, which got heavy fast. We hugged in the parking lot for a long time and promised not to let it go another five years, which we have promised before.

I've decided I'm changing it again next month, and this time I'm telling everyone.

We drove past the old house today, the one on Maple where I grew up, and someone painted it this awful mustard yellow. My dad would have lost his mind. He spent a whole summer painting it blue. Oh, that reminds me, put it in my notes that Dad's birthday dinner is at Luigi's on the twelfth, my sister already booked it. And then we drove past the high school and the football field has turf now, which feels wrong somehow, we used to play in actual mud. The diner across the street is a vape shop now too. Everything I remember is a vape shop. My kids think I'm making it up when I say we used to ride bikes to the pond and stay out until the streetlights came on. My son asked if the streetlights were connected to wifi. I didn't even know how to answer that. I just turned the radio up.

We have a toddler and a lot of electronics.

Hey, what did I say the contractor's name was? The guy who came out to look at the roof last month. I think it started with a D, maybe Dennis or Doug. So today was strange. I got to the bakery at six like always, and the oven wouldn't light. Ramon, the repair guy, came by around eight and said the igniter was shot and the part would be ninety four dollars. We ended up selling only muffins until noon, and somehow people loved it. One lady, Mrs. Abernathy, who comes in every Tuesday for a rye loaf, said she'd been telling us for years we should do a muffin day. A kid from the high school asked if we'd ever do blueberry lemon. By eleven we had sold out of everything but the bran ones, which nobody ever wants anyway. Ramon says the part should come in by Thursday, so tomorrow is apparently muffin day again whether I like it or not.

I'm going to stop in tomorrow, I think. My husband says I'm too much of a creature of habit, which, fair. I eat the same breakfast every day, oatmeal with blueberries, and I've had the same haircut since college. But I don't know, routines make me feel calm. And with three kids and a job and my dad's health stuff, I need something to feel calm about. Anyway, I'm rambling. What do you think, is it bad to be a creature of habit, or is it just how some people are wired?

We're trying to figure out what to do with the basement. It's about six hundred square feet, unfinished, concrete floor, one small window. My husband wants a home gym. I want a guest room for when my parents visit from Ohio twice a year. The kids want a game room. Today I subbed for a fourth grade class at Lincoln Elementary for the first time. The regular teacher, Ms. Ferraro, left me a plan that was eleven pages long, color coded, with a seating chart and notes on every kid. There was a boy named Theo who asked if I knew that octopuses have three hearts, and then spent the whole science block explaining it to the class better than I ever could have.
